jobInfo.writeUp:
Upon arrival, homeowner stated the furnace was throwing a code. It would run for a couple minutes and then shut down. This is a rental home and it currently has no tenant in it. I found the unit fire with very weak and low flame. I found that there was next to no gas pressure coming out of gas valve. I verify there was gas coming in and gas valve will need to be replaced. I also found that the burner on the end that holds the flame sensor had no fuel coming out of it at all, and the burners are very dirty along with the orifice. I found the filter completely trashed and should’ve been changed a long time ago. I found a dirty blower assembly as well. The entire furnace cabinet is completely dirty and is more likely the cause of the clogged orifice. Return drop is full of dirt and debris. It was not able to run furnace to verify heat exchanger or combustion.

candidates.writeUp:
LHP was dispatched due to an issue with a light socket. Upon arrival, the homeowner expressed that she was unhappy with the existing light fixture and wanted to replace it with an integrated LED fixture. We provided the option to install a new dimmer switch along with a light fixture supplied by our company.

While completing the work, I noticed an existing subpanel in the home that was identified as a recalled Federal Pacific electrical panel. These panels are known for potential breaker failure, including breakers that may not trip when required. This creates a significant safety concern due to the increased risk of overheating and electrical fires.

I informed the homeowner of the potential hazards associated with the recalled panel and explained that, due to the known safety concerns, we are obligated to bring this issue to her attention and provide a recommended solution.

All work
